Who this practice is for

This short refresher helps students rebuild coordinate-geometry foundations before or during university mathematics. It can also support learners at earlier stages who are revisiting these techniques; it is not tied to an exam board.

Four practice pages combine quick reminders, examples and working space, followed by two pages of complete worked answers. Attempt the questions before checking the answers and note any skills that need more practice.

6 pages · 13 questions · Aim: 30 minutes · Worked answers

Topics covered

  • Gradient between two points and the vertical-line exception
  • Midpoint and distance, including exact surds
  • Reading and writing y = mx + c
  • Equations through a known point or two points
  • Intersections of two straight lines

Prerequisites: basic algebra, coordinates and Pythagoras. This is a short skills refresher, not a complete coordinate-geometry course or an exam paper. The 30-minute target is a flexible practice aim, not a validated test duration.

Key ideas at a glance

Keep coordinate differences in the same order

Use m = (y₂ - y₁)/(x₂ - x₁), with x₂ ≠ x₁. If the x-coordinates are equal, the line is vertical and its gradient is undefined.

Use one point to find the equation

With gradient m and point (x₁, y₁), use y - y₁ = m(x - x₁). For an intersection, set the two expressions for y equal and substitute the resulting x into either equation.
